docs.title: frac_blp
docs.text:
FRAC for macro-BLP (Salanie-Wolak).

  • Github repository: https://github.com/bsalanie/frac-blp/
  • Documentation https://bsalanie.github.io/frac-blp/

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The package estimates a second-order approximation to the macro BLP model with random coefficients using the FRAC method of Salanie and Wolak.

At this early stage, the package only implements the basic version of the model without demographics. The random coefficients are assumed to be independently distributed.

The user should be familiar with the macro BLP model (Berry, Levinsohn, and Pakes, 1995). We use very similar notation to that of Conlon and Gortmaker in their pyblp package.

docs.title: inputs
docs.text:
The user must provide the inputs in a TOML configuration file. Here is an example: 

[data]
source = "real"                   # indicates that it is data from observations
file = "data/simulated_data.csv"   # must be .csv or .parquet
shares = "shares"                 # the name of the column that contains the market shares $S_{jt}$
# the names of the columns that have the instrumments. A constant is added automatically; do not list one
instruments = ["z_1", "z_2", "z_3"]  
# 
X1_exo = ["constant"]
X1_endo = ["x_1", "x_2", "x_3"] 
X2_exo = []                           # must be a subset of X1_exo
X2_endo = ["x_1", "x_2"]              # must be a subset of X1_endo
T = 500                               # number of markets
J = 10                                # number of products on each market

[estimation]
degree_Z = 2                          
# we create instruments from interactions of the `instruments` up to `degree_Z` 
degree_X1 = 2                         #   interacted with powers of `X1_exo` up to `degree_X1`
optimal_instruments = true            #   if `true`, we use the optimal instruments
run_projections = true                #   if `true`, some information about the first stage is printed
results_file = "estimation_results.txt"         # this is the default value.
The file must have one row per product and market, stacked by market (N=T * J rows, where T is the number of markets and J is the number of products per market) The observations should be ordered by market, i.e., the first J rows correspond to market 1, the next J rows to market 2, etc. The path of file is relative to that of the configuration file.

The names of the variables must correspond to column names in the header of file.

The program will construct the following Numpy matrices from the data, using the column names indicated in the configuration file: * X1_exo, the matrix of exogenous variables with fixed coefficients * X1_endo, the matrix of endogenous variables with fixed coefficients * X2_exo, the matrix of exogenous variables with fixed coefficients * X1_endo, the matrix of endogenous variables with fixed coefficients.

X2_exo must be a subset of X1_exo, and X2_endo must be a subset of X1_endo (i.e., all variables with random coefficients must also have fixed coefficients). Any of these four matrices can be None if there are no variables of that type.

A constant term will not be added automatically. If one is desired, the user must include a column of ones in X1_exo, and in X2_exo if the coefficient of the constant is random.

On the other hand, a constant will be added automatically to the instruments. If degree_Z=d is provided, then all interactions of the \(n_Z\) columns of Z up to degree d, plus the constant, will be used as instruments. This gives \({n_Z+d\choose d}\) instruments. If degree_X1=d' is provided, then all interactions of the \(n_{1x}\) columns of X1_exo up to degree d' will also be used, on their own and multiplied by the interactions of Z up to degree d. That gives an additional \(({n_Z+d\choose d}-1)\times ({n_{1x}+d^\prime\choose d^\prime}-1)+1\) instruments.

The default has degree_Z=2 and degree_X1=2; the total number of instruments then is: $$ \frac{(n_{1x}+1)(n_{1x}+2)}{2} \times \left(\frac{(n_{Z}+1)(n_{Z}+2)}{2}-1\right). $$

docs.title: outputs
docs.text:
The outputs are:

  • betas_sigmas2_est: the estimates of the mean coefficients on the variables X1_exo and X1_endo, then the estimated variances of the coefficients on X2_exo and X2_endo, in that order.
  • stderrs_est: the estimated standard errors of these estimates.
  • xi_est: the estimated product effects, a vector of size N, ordered by market

They are saved in the text file indicated as results_file in the configuration file. If no results_file is indicated, the results are written in estimation_results.txt. Its path is relative to where the program was run.

docs.title: config module
docs.text:
Read FRAC estimation settings and data from a TOML configuration file.

The file has three sections:

  • [data]: where the data come from. With source = "real", the data are read from a CSV or Parquet file; with source = "simulated", they are simulated.
  • [simulation]: parameters of the simulation, used when source = "simulated".
  • [estimation]: options for frac_nodemog_estimate.

Relative paths for file are taken relative to the directory of the config file.

class DataConfig(_StrictModel):
    """The ``[data]`` section.

    Attributes:
        source (str): ``"real"`` to read a file, ``"simulated"`` to simulate.
        file (Path | None): Path to a CSV or Parquet file with one row per product
            and market, stacked by market. Needed for ``source = "real"``.
        shares (str | None): Column with the observed shares.
        instruments (list[str]): Columns of the instruments. A constant is added
            automatically, so do not include one.
        X1_exo (list[str]): Columns of the exogenous regressors with fixed coefficients.
        X1_endo (list[str]): Columns of the endogenous regressors with fixed coefficients.
        X2_exo (list[str]): Columns of the exogenous regressors with random
            coefficients. Must be a subset of ``X1_exo``.
        X2_endo (list[str]): Columns of the endogenous regressors with random
            coefficients. Must be a subset of ``X1_endo``.
        T (int | None): Number of markets. Needed for ``source = "real"``.
        J (int | None): Number of products per market. Needed for ``source = "real"``.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    source: Literal["real", "simulated"]
    file: Path | None = None
    shares: str | None = None
    instruments: list[str] = []
    X1_exo: list[str] = []
    X1_endo: list[str] = []
    X2_exo: list[str] = []
    X2_endo: list[str] = []
    T: int | None = None
    J: int | None = None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check_real_fields(self) -> "DataConfig":
        """Check that the fields needed for real data are given and do not clash.

        Returns:
            DataConfig: The validated section, unchanged.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If a field needed for real data is missing, or if a
                regressor is listed in both its exogenous and endogenous lists,
                or an ``X2`` name is not in the matching ``X1`` list.
        """
        if self.source == "real":
            missing = [
                name
                for name in ("file", "shares", "T", "J")
                if getattr(self, name) is None
            ]
            if not self.instruments:
                missing.append("instruments")
            if missing:
                raise ValueError(f"[data] with source = 'real' needs: {missing}")
            both = sorted(set(self.X1_exo) & set(self.X1_endo))
            if both:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"[data] lists {both} in both X1_exo and X1_endo; "
                    "each regressor must be in exactly one of them."
                )
            both_X2 = sorted(set(self.X2_exo) & set(self.X2_endo))
            if both_X2:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"[data] lists {both_X2} in both X2_exo and X2_endo; "
                    "each regressor must be in exactly one of them."
                )
            not_in_exo = [name for name in self.X2_exo if name not in self.X1_exo]
            if not_in_exo:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"[data] X2_exo {not_in_exo} must be in X1_exo {self.X1_exo}."
                )
            not_in_endo = [name for name in self.X2_endo if name not in self.X1_endo]
            if not_in_endo:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"[data] X2_endo {not_in_endo} must be in X1_endo {self.X1_endo}."
                )
        return self

def build_frac_data(config: Config) -> FracNoDemogData:
    """Build the FRAC data object described by a configuration.

    Args:
        config (Config): Settings from :func:`load_config`.

    Returns:
        FracNoDemogData: Simulated data, or real data read from ``data.file``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the file lacks some of the named columns or does not have
            ``T * J`` rows.
    """
    if config.data.source == "simulated":
        sim = config.simulation
        return simulate_frac_nodemog_data(
            T=sim.T,
            J=sim.J,
            n_X1_exo=sim.n_X1_exo,
            n_X1_endo=sim.n_X1_endo,
            n_X2_exo=sim.n_X2_exo,
            n_X2_endo=sim.n_X2_endo,
            sigma_x=sim.sigma_x,
            sigma_xi=sim.sigma_xi,
            rho_x_xi=sim.rho_x_xi,
            rho_x_z=sim.rho_x_z,
            betas=np.array(sim.betas),
            sigmas=np.array(sim.sigmas),
            seed=sim.seed,
        )

    data = config.data
    assert data.file is not None and data.shares is not None
    assert data.T is not None and data.J is not None
    df = _read_table(data.file)

    names_X1 = data.X1_exo + data.X1_endo
    needed = [data.shares, *data.instruments, *names_X1]
    missing = [name for name in needed if name not in df.columns]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"Columns missing from {data.file}: {missing}")
    if len(df) != data.T * data.J:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{data.file} has {len(df)} rows, but T * J = {data.T * data.J}."
        )

    frac_real_data = FracNoDemogRealData(
        T=data.T,
        J=data.J,
        df_X1=df[names_X1].copy(),
        Z=df[data.instruments].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64),
        shares=df[data.shares].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64),
        names_X1_exo=data.X1_exo,
        names_X1_endo=data.X1_endo,
        names_X2_exo=data.X2_exo,
        names_X2_endo=data.X2_endo,
    )
    return frac_real_data

def load_config(path: str | Path) -> Config:
    """Read and validate a TOML configuration file.

    Args:
        path (str | Path): Path to the TOML file.

    Returns:
        Config: The validated settings. A relative ``data.file`` is resolved
        against the directory of the config file.

    Raises:
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the file has unknown keys or invalid values.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    with path.open("rb") as f:
        raw = tomllib.load(f)
    config = Config.model_validate(raw)
    if config.data.file is not None and not config.data.file.is_absolute():
        config.data.file = path.parent / config.data.file
    return config

def run_example(
    T: int = 50,
    J: int = 20,
    n_X1_exo: int = 1,
    n_X1_endo: int = 1,
    n_X2_exo: int = 0,
    n_X2_endo: int = 1,
    sigma_x: float = 1.0,
    sigma_xi: float = 1.0,
    rho_x_xi: float = np.sqrt(0.5),
    rho_x_z: float = np.sqrt(0.5),
    betas: np.ndarray = np.array([-4.3, 1.0]),
    sigmas: np.ndarray = np.array([1.0]),
) -> None:
    """Simulate data and estimate it with FRAC without demographics.

    Then repeat the estimation using the interface for real data.

    Args:
        T (int): Number of markets. Default is 50.
        J (int): Number of products per market. Default is 20.
        n_X1_exo (int): Number of exogenous regressors with fixed coefficients,
            including the constant. Default is 1.
        n_X1_endo (int): Number of endogenous regressors with fixed coefficients.
            Default is 1.
        n_X2_exo (int): Number of exogenous regressors with random coefficients.
            Default is 0.
        n_X2_endo (int): Number of endogenous regressors with random coefficients.
            Default is 1.
        sigma_x (float): Standard deviation parameter of the regressors. Default is 1.0.
        sigma_xi (float): Standard deviation of the unobserved product characteristic.
            Default is 1.0.
        rho_x_xi (float): Correlation between the regressors and the unobserved
            characteristic. Default is sqrt(0.5).
        rho_x_z (float): Correlation between the regressors and the instruments.
            Default is sqrt(0.5).
        betas (np.ndarray): Fixed coefficients. Default is ``[-4.3, 1.0]``.
        sigmas (np.ndarray): Standard deviations of the random coefficients.
            Default is ``[1.0]``.
    """
    print_stars("Hello from frac_blp!")
    simulated_frac_data = simulate_frac_nodemog_data(
        T=T,
        J=J,
        n_X1_exo=n_X1_exo,
        n_X1_endo=n_X1_endo,
        n_X2_exo=n_X2_exo,
        n_X2_endo=n_X2_endo,
        sigma_x=sigma_x,
        sigma_xi=sigma_xi,
        rho_x_xi=rho_x_xi,
        rho_x_z=rho_x_z,
        betas=betas,
        sigmas=sigmas,
    )
    print_stars("Simulated Data:")
    print(simulated_frac_data)

    print_stars("Estimating with FRAC")
    _, _ = frac_nodemog_estimate(simulated_frac_data, degree_Z=3, degree_X1=3)

    print_stars("Example with the real data interface:")
    df_X1 = pd.DataFrame(
        np.column_stack(
            (
                simulated_frac_data.X1_exo,
                simulated_frac_data.X1_endo,
            )
        ),
        columns=simulated_frac_data.names_X1,
    )
    real_frac_data = FracNoDemogRealData(
        T=simulated_frac_data.T,
        J=simulated_frac_data.J,
        df_X1=df_X1,
        Z=simulated_frac_data.Z,
        names_X1_exo=simulated_frac_data.names_X1_exo,
        names_X1_endo=simulated_frac_data.names_X1_endo,
        names_X2_exo=simulated_frac_data.names_X2_exo,
        names_X2_endo=simulated_frac_data.names_X2_endo,
        shares=simulated_frac_data.shares,
    )
    print_stars("Estimating with FRAC")
    _, _ = frac_nodemog_estimate(real_frac_data, degree_Z=3, degree_X1=3)

@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def gauss_hermite_grid(dim: int, points_per_dim: int) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Return tensor Gauss-Hermite nodes and normalized weights for N(0, I).

    The result depends only on ``dim`` and ``points_per_dim``, so it is cached.
    The returned arrays are shared between calls and must not be modified.

    Args:
        dim (int): Number of dimensions.
        points_per_dim (int): Number of quadrature points in each dimension.

    Returns:
        tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]: ``standard_nodes``, a
        ``(points_per_dim**dim, dim)`` array of nodes, and ``standard_weights``,
        a ``(points_per_dim**dim,)`` array of weights that sum to 1.
    """
    # 1. Get 1D physicists' Gauss-Hermite nodes and strictly positive weights
    # They integrate against the weight function w(x) = exp(-x^2)
    x_1d, w_1d = roots_hermite(points_per_dim)

    # 2. Build the multi-dimensional grid using meshgrid
    mesh_args = [x_1d] * dim
    grids = np.meshgrid(*mesh_args, indexing="ij")
    standard_nodes = np.stack([g.ravel() for g in grids], axis=-1)

    # 3. Build the multi-dimensional weights (outer product of 1D weights)
    w_grids = np.meshgrid(*[w_1d] * dim, indexing="ij")
    standard_weights = np.prod(np.stack([w.ravel() for w in w_grids], axis=-1), axis=1)

    # Normalize weights so they sum up to 1 (converting physicists' weights to a probability distribution)
    # The weight function for physicists' Hermite is exp(-x^2), but normal distributions use exp(-x^2/2) / sqrt(2*pi)
    standard_weights = standard_weights / (np.pi ** (dim / 2))
    return standard_nodes, standard_weights

def integrate_gaussian(
    f: Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray | float],
    dim_f: int,
    mu: np.ndarray,
    sigma: np.ndarray,
    points_per_dim: int = 5,
) -> np.ndarray | float:
    """Integrate f(X) for X ~ N(mu, sigma) by tensor Gauss-Hermite quadrature.

    Supports up to 5 dimensions. The quadrature weights are positive.

    Args:
        f (Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray | float]): Function of one
            node, a ``(dim,)`` array. Returns a scalar if ``dim_f`` is 1, and
            a ``(dim_f,)`` array otherwise.
        dim_f (int): Dimension of the output of ``f``. Use 1 for a scalar.
        mu (np.ndarray): Mean of the Gaussian, a ``(dim,)`` array.
        sigma (np.ndarray): Covariance matrix of the Gaussian, a ``(dim, dim)``
            positive definite array.
        points_per_dim (int): Number of quadrature points in each dimension.
            Default is 5.

    Returns:
        np.ndarray | float: The integral of ``f``: a scalar if ``dim_f`` is 1,
        and a ``(dim_f,)`` array otherwise.

    Raises:
        AssertionError: If ``mu`` has more than 5 elements.
    """
    dim = len(mu)
    assert dim <= 5, "This specific grid generation script is optimized for d <= 5"

    standard_nodes, standard_weights = gauss_hermite_grid(dim, points_per_dim)

    # 4. Transform nodes from Standard Normal space to the target Gaussian N(mu, sigma)
    # Handle covariance via Cholesky decomposition: X = mu + L * (sqrt(2) * standard_nodes)
    L = np.linalg.cholesky(sigma)
    transformed_nodes = mu + (np.sqrt(2) * standard_nodes) @ L.T

    # 5. Evaluate function and calculate the dot product
    # Every single weight in 'standard_weights' is strictly >
    if dim_f == 1:
        f_values = np.array([f(node) for node in transformed_nodes])
        integral = np.dot(f_values, standard_weights)
    else:
        f_values = np.zeros((dim_f, transformed_nodes.shape[0]))
        for i_node, node in enumerate(transformed_nodes):
            f_values[:, i_node] = f(node)
        integral = np.dot(f_values, standard_weights)

    return cast(np.ndarray | float, integral)

docs.title: frac_expansions module
docs.text:
Small-sigma expansion of the BLP inversion xi_j(S, X; sigma, c, s, kappa).

Model: beta_i = b + sigma * eps_i, with eps_{il} independent across l, E eps_l = 0, E eps_l^2 = sigma^2_l, E eps_l^3 = sigma_l^3 * s_l, E eps_l^4 = sigma_l^4 * (3 + kappa_l).

for the logit share function s(delta),

s_j(delta + X t) / s_j(delta) = exp(t'X_j - K(t)),

where K is the cumulant generating function of the characteristics X under the distribution of shares on {0, ..., J} (with X_0 = 0). Hence ln(S_j / S_0) = delta_j + L_j - L_0, L_j = ln E exp(sigma eps'y_j - [K(sigma eps) - sigma eps'e]), with y_j = X_j - e (e = (e_1, ..., e_k)). A cumulant expansion of L_j, followed by replacing the logit shares s(delta) by the observed S, gives xi_j to order sigma^4.

The result is written in raw share-weighted moments of X over the inside goods (the outside good has X_0 = 0, so it contributes nothing), evaluated at the observed S: e_l = sum_j S_j X_jl, e_2l = sum_j S_j X_jl^2, e_3l = sum_j S_j X_jl^3, v_lm = sum_j S_j X_jl X_jm - e_l e_m.

def xi_terms(
    S: np.ndarray,
    X: np.ndarray,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Return the successive terms of the expansion of xi on all markets.

    xi = y - X*b - term2 * sigmas^2 - term3 * s *  sigmas^3
        - (sigmas^2)' * term4_gaussian * sigmas^2 - term4_kappa * sigmas^4 + O(sigmas^5)

    Args:
        S (np.ndarray): Inside shares, a (T, J) matrix with one row per market.
        X (np.ndarray): Characteristics with random coefficients, a (T, J, K) array.

    Returns:
        tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]: ``term2``, a (T, J, K)
        array of order 2 terms; ``term3``, a (T, J, K) array of order 3 terms;
        ``term4_gaussian``, a (T, J, K, K) array of Gaussian order 4 terms; and
        ``term4_kappa``, a (T, J, K) array of order 4 terms from excess kurtosis.
    """
    X2 = X * X
    X3 = X2 * X
    # market-level moments, each a (T, K) matrix
    e1 = np.einsum("tj,tjk->tk", S, X)
    e2 = np.einsum("tj,tjk->tk", S, X2)
    e3 = np.einsum("tj,tjk->tk", S, X3)
    v = np.einsum("tj,tjl,tjm->tlm", S, X, X) - np.einsum("tl,tm->tlm", e1, e1)
    # broadcast the market-level moments over the J products
    e1, e2, e3 = e1[:, None, :], e2[:, None, :], e3[:, None, :]

    # order 2:  sum_l (sigma^2_l * term2_l)
    term2 = X * (X / 2.0 - e1)

    # order 3:  sum_l (sigma_l^3 * s_l * term3_l)
    term3 = X * (X2 / 6.0 - X * e1 / 2 + e1**2 - e2 / 2.0)

    # order 4: sum_l sigma_l^4 * kappa_l * term4_kappa_l
    #                   + sum_{l,m} sigma_l^2 sigma_m^2 term4_gaussian_lm
    term4_kappa = X * (
        X3 / 24.0
        - e1 * X2 / 6.0
        + (e1**2 / 2.0 - e2 / 4.0) * X
        + e1 * e2
        - e1**3
        - e3 / 6
    )
    term4_gaussian = -np.einsum("tlm,tjl,tjm->tjlm", v, X, X / 2.0 - e1)

    return term2, term3, term4_gaussian, term4_kappa

def frac_nodemog_estimate(
    frac_data: FracNoDemogData,
    degree_Z: int = 2,
    degree_X1: int = 2,
    optimal_instruments: bool = True,
    run_projections: bool = True,
) -> ThreeArrays:
    """
    Estimate FRAC parameters without demographics using two-stage least squares.

    Args:
        frac_data (FracNoDemogData): Data container with regressors, instruments, and
            simulated or empirical shares.
        degree_Z (int): Degree of polynomial expansion for instruments. Default is 2.
        degree_X1 (int): Degree of polynomial expansion for exogenous regressors in X1.
            Default is 2.
        optimal_instruments (bool): If True, use optimal instruments. Default is True.
        run_projections (bool): If True, print the R-squared values of the first-stage
            projections on the instruments. Default is True.

    Returns:
        TwoArrays: Tuple ``(betas_sigmas_est, stderrs_est)``: the estimated fixed
        coefficients followed by the estimated variances of the random coefficients,
        and their standard errors.

    Raises:
        SystemExit: If one of the estimated variances is negative.
    """
    X1_exo = frac_data.X1_exo
    X1, X2 = frac_data.X1.astype(np.float64), frac_data.X2.astype(np.float64)
    J, T = frac_data.J, frac_data.T
    Z = frac_data.Z
    names_X1 = frac_data.names_X1
    names_X2 = frac_data.names_X2
    shares = frac_data.shares

    # print(f"{shares.min()=}, {shares.max()=}")

    y = make_y(shares, J)

    # term2 = X * (X / 2 - e1), with e1 = sum_j S_j X_j, computed for all markets at once
    S_all = shares.reshape((T, J))
    X2_all = X2.reshape((T, J, -1))
    e1 = np.einsum("tj,tjk->tk", S_all, X2_all)
    K = (X2_all * (X2_all / 2.0 - e1[:, None, :])).reshape(X2.shape)

    n_X1 = X1.shape[1]
    n_X2 = X2.shape[1]

    # combine exogenous regressors and instruments
    Z_full = make_Z_full(Z, X1_exo, degree_Z=degree_Z, degree_X1=degree_X1).astype(
        np.float64
    )

    # combine covariates and artificial regressors
    X = np.column_stack((X1, K))

    # project X on the full set of instruments, once: used for the R2s and by TSLS
    X_proj, _, r2_X = proj_on_Z(X, Z_full)

    if run_projections:
        _, _, r2_y = proj_on_Z(y.reshape((frac_data.n_obs, 1)), Z_full)
        r2_X1, r2_K = r2_X[:n_X1], r2_X[n_X1:]

        print_stars(
            f"The first stage R2s of projecting on the full set of {Z_full.shape[1]} instruments are:"
        )
        print(f"    for y: {r2_y[0]:.3f}")
        for ix in range(n_X1):
            print(f"     for {names_X1[ix]}: {r2_X1[ix]:.3f}")
        for ix in range(n_X2):
            print(f"     for K_{names_X2[ix]}: {r2_K[ix]:.3f}")
        print("\n")

    # run TSLS
    print_stars("Running TSLS...")
    betas_sigmas2_est, betas_sigmas2_varest, xi_est = tsls_estimate(
        y,
        X,
        Z_full,
        J,
        optimal_instruments,
        prev_residuals=None,
        X_proj=X_proj,
    )
    sigmas_squared_est = betas_sigmas2_est[n_X1:]
    if np.min(sigmas_squared_est) < 0.0:
        print_stars("\n The variance estimates are")
        print(sigmas_squared_est)
        print_stars("We have a negative variance estimate!")

    stderrs_est = np.sqrt(np.diag(betas_sigmas2_varest))

    print_tsls_results(
        betas_sigmas2_est,
        stderrs_est,
        names_coeffs=names_X1 + ["sigma2_" + name for name in names_X2],
        title="The FRAC second-order estimates are:",
    )

    return betas_sigmas2_est, stderrs_est, xi_est

def make_X(X_exo: np.ndarray | None, X_endo: np.ndarray | None) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Combine exogenous and endogenous regressors into a single regressor matrix.

    Args:
        X_exo (np.ndarray | None): Exogenous regressors.
        X_endo (np.ndarray | None): Endogenous regressors.

    Returns:
        np.ndarray: The concatenated regressor matrix.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If both `X_exo` and `X_endo` are ``None``.
    """
    if X_exo is not None and X_endo is not None:
        X = np.column_stack((X_exo, X_endo))
    elif X_exo is not None:
        X = X_exo
    elif X_endo is not None:
        X = X_endo
    else:
        raise ValueError("At least one of X_exo or X_endo must be provided.")
    return X

def make_Z_full(
    Z: np.ndarray,
    X1_exo: np.ndarray | None = None,
    degree_Z: int = 2,
    degree_X1: int = 2,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Build a full set of polynomial instruments for FRAC without demographics.

    Args:
        Z (np.ndarray): Baseline instruments.
        X1_exo (np.ndarray | None): Exogenous regressors without random coefficients.
        degree_Z (int): Maximum degree applied to columns of ``Z`` (must be >= 0).
        degree_X1 (int): Maximum degree applied to columns of ``X1_exo``.

    Returns:
        np.ndarray: Instrument matrix whose columns enumerate every admissible
        combination of polynomial terms, preceded by a column of ones.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``degree_Z`` is negative.
    """
    if degree_Z < 0:
        raise ValueError("degree_Z must be non-negative.")

    n_obs = Z.shape[0]
    effective_X1 = X1_exo if X1_exo is not None else np.ones((n_obs, 1))
    max_dx1 = degree_X1 if X1_exo is not None else 0

    columns: list[np.ndarray] = []
    for d_z in range(degree_Z + 1):
        for z_term in _monomials_of_degree(Z, d_z):
            for d_x1 in range(max_dx1 + 1):
                for x1_term in _monomials_of_degree(effective_X1, d_x1):
                    columns.append(z_term * x1_term)

    return np.column_stack(columns)

def make_centered_covariance(X: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Compute the centered covariance matrix of a given matrix.

    Args:
        X (np.ndarray): Input matrix with shape (n_samples, n_features).

    Returns:
        np.ndarray: Centered covariance matrix with shape (n_features, n_features).
    """
    n_samples = X.shape[0]
    X_centered = X - np.mean(X, axis=0)
    return cast(np.ndarray, (X_centered.T @ X_centered) / n_samples)

def make_y(shares: np.ndarray, J: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Create the dependent variable vector for FRAC estimation.

    Args:
        shares (np.ndarray): Market shares, a (T*J,) vector stacked by market.
        J (int): Number of products in each market.

    Returns:
        np.ndarray: The log of each share divided by the outside share
        of its market, with the same shape as ``shares``.
    """
    n_markets = shares.shape[0] // J
    shares_mat = shares.reshape((n_markets, J))
    # print(f"{shares_mat.min()=}", f"{shares_mat.max()=}")
    shares_zero = 1.0 - shares_mat.sum(axis=1)
    # print(f"{shares_zero.min()=}")
    y = np.log(shares_mat / shares_zero.reshape((-1, 1)))
    return cast(np.ndarray, y.reshape(shares.shape))

def mnl_probabilities(u: np.ndarray, outside: bool = False) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return the MNL probabilities for utilities u.

    Args:
        u (np.ndarray): Utilities of the J alternatives, a 1D array.
        outside (bool): If True, include an outside option with utility 0.

    Returns:
        np.ndarray: The J probabilities ``exp(u) / sum(exp(u))`` or, if
        ``outside`` is True, ``exp(u) / (1 + sum(exp(u)))``.
    """
    u = np.asarray(u)
    u_max = np.max(u)
    exp_u = np.exp(u - u_max)
    if outside:
        return np.asarray(exp_u / (np.exp(-u_max) + np.sum(exp_u)))
    return np.asarray(exp_u / np.sum(exp_u))

def proj_on_Z(
    X: np.ndarray, Z: np.ndarray
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """
    Project each column of ``X`` onto ``Z`` and report fitted values.

    Args:
        X (np.ndarray): Variables to project, an (n, K) matrix.
        Z (np.ndarray): Instruments used for the projections, an (n, L) matrix.

    Returns:
        tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]: ``X_proj``, an (n, K) matrix
        of projected columns; ``coef``, an (L, K) matrix of least-squares
        coefficients; and ``r2``, a K-vector of column-wise R-squared values.
    """
    EPS = 1e-12
    # one least-squares call handles all columns of X
    coef = spla.lstsq(Z, X)[0]
    X_proj = Z @ coef
    var_x = np.var(X, axis=0)
    var_x_proj = np.var(X_proj, axis=0)
    # columns with (numerically) zero variance get r2 = 1, as before
    safe_var_x = np.where(var_x < EPS, 1.0, var_x)
    r2 = np.where(var_x < EPS, 1.0, var_x_proj / safe_var_x)
    return X_proj, coef, r2

@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def gauss_hermite_grid(dim: int, points_per_dim: int) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Return tensor Gauss-Hermite nodes and normalized weights for N(0, I).

    The result depends only on ``dim`` and ``points_per_dim``, so it is cached.
    The returned arrays are shared between calls and must not be modified.

    Args:
        dim (int): Number of dimensions.
        points_per_dim (int): Number of quadrature points in each dimension.

    Returns:
        tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]: ``standard_nodes``, a
        ``(points_per_dim**dim, dim)`` array of nodes, and ``standard_weights``,
        a ``(points_per_dim**dim,)`` array of weights that sum to 1.
    """
    # 1. Get 1D physicists' Gauss-Hermite nodes and strictly positive weights
    # They integrate against the weight function w(x) = exp(-x^2)
    x_1d, w_1d = roots_hermite(points_per_dim)

    # 2. Build the multi-dimensional grid using meshgrid
    mesh_args = [x_1d] * dim
    grids = np.meshgrid(*mesh_args, indexing="ij")
    standard_nodes = np.stack([g.ravel() for g in grids], axis=-1)

    # 3. Build the multi-dimensional weights (outer product of 1D weights)
    w_grids = np.meshgrid(*[w_1d] * dim, indexing="ij")
    standard_weights = np.prod(np.stack([w.ravel() for w in w_grids], axis=-1), axis=1)

    # Normalize weights so they sum up to 1 (converting physicists' weights to a probability distribution)
    # The weight function for physicists' Hermite is exp(-x^2), but normal distributions use exp(-x^2/2) / sqrt(2*pi)
    standard_weights = standard_weights / (np.pi ** (dim / 2))
    return standard_nodes, standard_weights

    points_per_dim: int = 5,
) -> np.ndarray | float:
    """Integrate f(X) for X ~ N(mu, sigma) by tensor Gauss-Hermite quadrature.

    Supports up to 5 dimensions. The quadrature weights are positive.

    Args:
        f (Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray | float]): Function of one
            node, a ``(dim,)`` array. Returns a scalar if ``dim_f`` is 1, and
            a ``(dim_f,)`` array otherwise.
        dim_f (int): Dimension of the output of ``f``. Use 1 for a scalar.
        mu (np.ndarray): Mean of the Gaussian, a ``(dim,)`` array.
        sigma (np.ndarray): Covariance matrix of the Gaussian, a ``(dim, dim)``
            positive definite array.
        points_per_dim (int): Number of quadrature points in each dimension.
            Default is 5.

    Returns:
        np.ndarray | float: The integral of ``f``: a scalar if ``dim_f`` is 1,
        and a ``(dim_f,)`` array otherwise.

    Raises:
        AssertionError: If ``mu`` has more than 5 elements.
    """
    dim = len(mu)
    assert dim <= 5, "This specific grid generation script is optimized for d <= 5"

    standard_nodes, standard_weights = gauss_hermite_grid(dim, points_per_dim)

    # 4. Transform nodes from Standard Normal space to the target Gaussian N(mu, sigma)
    # Handle covariance via Cholesky decomposition: X = mu + L * (sqrt(2) * standard_nodes)
    L = np.linalg.cholesky(sigma)
    transformed_nodes = mu + (np.sqrt(2) * standard_nodes) @ L.T

    # 5. Evaluate function and calculate the dot product
    # Every single weight in 'standard_weights' is strictly >
    if dim_f == 1:
        f_values = np.array([f(node) for node in transformed_nodes])
        integral = np.dot(f_values, standard_weights)
    else:
        f_values = np.zeros((dim_f, transformed_nodes.shape[0]))
        for i_node, node in enumerate(transformed_nodes):
            f_values[:, i_node] = f(node)
        integral = np.dot(f_values, standard_weights)

    return cast(np.ndarray | float, integral)

def my_function(x: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Return the sum of squares of the coordinates of a point.

    Args:
        x (np.ndarray): A point, a vector of shape (d,).

    """
    return float(np.sum(x**2))

def simulate_frac_nodemog_data(
    T: int = 50,
    J: int = 20,
    n_X1_exo: int = 1,
    n_X1_endo: int = 1,
    n_X2_exo: int = 0,
    n_X2_endo: int = 1,
    sigma_x: float = 1.0,
    sigma_xi: float = 1.0,
    rho_x_xi: float = np.sqrt(0.5),
    rho_x_z: float = np.sqrt(0.5),
    betas: np.ndarray = np.array([-4.3, 1.0]),
    sigmas: np.ndarray = np.array([1.0]),
    seed: int | None = None,
) -> FracNoDemogSimulatedData:
    """
    Simulate FRAC data with endogenous random-coefficient regressors.

    Args:
        seed (int | None): Seed for the random draws. If None, each run gives different data.

    Returns:
        FracNoDemogSimulatedData: Simulated dataset ready for FRAC estimation.
    """
    n_X1 = n_X1_exo + n_X1_endo
    n_X2 = n_X2_exo + n_X2_endo
    names_X1_exo = ["constant"]
    if n_X1_exo > 1:
        names_X1_exo += [f"x_{i + 1}" for i in range(n_X1_exo - 1)]
    names_X1_endo = [f"x_{i}" for i in range(n_X1_exo, n_X1)]
    names_X2_exo = [f"x_{i + 1}" for i in range(n_X2_exo)]
    names_X2_endo = [f"x_{i + 1}" for i in range(n_X2_exo, n_X2)]

    return FracNoDemogSimulatedData(
        T=T,
        J=J,
        names_X1_exo=names_X1_exo,
        names_X1_endo=names_X1_endo,
        names_X2_exo=names_X2_exo,
        names_X2_endo=names_X2_endo,
        sigma_x=sigma_x,
        sigma_xi=sigma_xi,
        rho_x_z=rho_x_z,
        rho_x_xi=rho_x_xi,
        betas=betas,
        sigmas=sigmas,
        seed=seed,
    )

def print_tsls_results(
    estimated_coeffs: np.ndarray,
    estimated_stderrs: np.ndarray,
    names_coeffs: list[str] | None = None,
    title: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """
    Print the estimated coefficients and their standard errors.

    Args:
        estimated_coeffs (np.ndarray): Estimated coefficients.
        estimated_stderrs (np.ndarray): Estimated standard errors.
        names_coeffs (list[str] | None): Coefficient names. If None, the
            coefficients are labeled ``coeff_0``, ``coeff_1``, ...
        title (str | None): Header printed above the results. If None,
            ``"Two-stage least squares estimates:"`` is used.
    """
    n_coeffs = estimated_coeffs.size
    if names_coeffs is None:
        names_coeffs = [f"coeff_{i}" for i in range(n_coeffs)]
    if title is None:
        title = "Two-stage least squares estimates:"
    print_stars(title)
    for i in range(len(names_coeffs)):
        print(
            f"   {names_coeffs[i]}: {estimated_coeffs[i]:.3f} (std err: {estimated_stderrs[i]:.3f})"
        )

def tsls_estimate(
    y: np.ndarray,
    X: np.ndarray,
    Z: np.ndarray,
    J: int,
    optimal_instruments: bool = True,
    prev_residuals: np.ndarray | None = None,
    X_proj: np.ndarray | None = None,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """
    Estimate $E(y - X\theta | Z) = 0$ by 2SLS with optimal instruments and weighting matrix.

    The previous residuals are used to estimate the within-market covariance
    of the errors, which gives the optimal instruments and the weighting matrix.

    Args:
        y (np.ndarray): Dependent variable, a (T*J,) vector.
        X (np.ndarray): Regressors, a (T*J, K) matrix.
        Z (np.ndarray): Instruments, a (T*J, L) matrix.
        J (int): Number of products in each market.
        optimal_instruments (bool): If True, use optimal instruments. Default is True.
        prev_residuals (np.ndarray | None): Previous residuals, a (T*J,) vector.
            If None, the OLS residuals of ``y`` on ``X`` are used.
        X_proj (np.ndarray | None): Projection of ``X`` onto ``Z``, a (T*J, K) matrix.
            If None, it is computed here. Pass it in to avoid recomputing it.

    Returns:
        tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]: The estimated coefficients
        (a K-vector), their estimated variance (a (K, K) matrix), and the new
        residuals (a (T*J,) vector).
    """
    if prev_residuals is None:  # we use the OLS residuals
        ols_est = np.linalg.lstsq(X, y, rcond=None)[0]
        prev_residuals = y - X @ ols_est

    # First stage: project X onto Z
    if X_proj is None:
        X_proj = proj_on_Z(X, Z)[0]

    n_obs, n_x = X.shape

    if optimal_instruments:
        D_mat = -X_proj
        Z_opt = D_mat
    else:
        Z_opt = Z

    # and the W weighting matrix
    Z_opt_moments = Z_opt * prev_residuals.reshape((-1, 1))
    W_mat = make_centered_covariance(Z_opt_moments)
    W_inv = np.linalg.pinv(W_mat)

    # W_inv: np.ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], np.dtype[np.float64]] = np.eye(n_x)  # --- IGNORE --- for testing only

    ZX = Z_opt.T @ X / n_obs
    ZXT = ZX.T
    Zy = Z_opt.T @ y / n_obs
    theta_est = np.linalg.solve(ZXT @ W_inv @ ZX, ZXT @ W_inv @ Zy)

    new_residuals = y - X @ theta_est

    theta_est_var = np.linalg.inv(ZXT @ W_inv @ ZX) / n_obs

    return theta_est, theta_est_var, new_residuals
